title: What is the area of this rectangle?
description: The sides of a rectangle are mixed numbers of feet. They are written as fractions and multiplied, with common factors divided out first.
teaching_notes: One idea: write each mixed number as a fraction, then divide out common factors before multiplying to get the area. Watch for students who multiply the whole parts and the fraction parts separately.

video_script.why: The child uses the divide out common factors method of the solved example to find an area.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question, a rectangle with sides three and three quarters feet and nine and three fifths feet
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with its two sides labelled in feet
video_script.payoff_line: The area of the rectangle is thirty six square feet
maths_rules: 15 and 5 share the factor 5: 3 and 1; 48 and 4 share the factor 4: 12 and 1
check: 3 3/4 is a little less than 4 and 9 3/5 a little less than 10, so the area is a little less than 40
video_script.design: A rectangle with the two sides labelled as mixed numbers. The working board changes each side to a fraction and then divides out the common factors.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a rectangle with the sides labelled three and three quarters feet, and nine and three fifths feet

marks.sides: the rectangle arrives with both sides labelled in feet
marks.ask: a question mark glows inside the rectangle

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>Its sides are three and three quarters feet, and nine and three fifths feet.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the rectangle?

beats.on_screen: the rectangle stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a rectangle with length and breadth marked; a pair of numbers linked by a line

marks.rule: the length and the breadth are outlined
marks.area: the area is written as length multiplied by breadth
marks.look: a top and a bottom with a common factor are linked by a line

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The area of a rectangle is its length multiplied by its breadth.
<bookmark mark='look'/>Before multiplying, we check every top against every bottom for a common factor.

marks.given: the two sides are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sides are three and three quarters feet, and nine and three fifths feet.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of the rectangle

marks.find: the words To find and the area are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the rectangle.

marks.first: the first side is written as quarters
marks.second: the second side is written as fifths

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, write each side as a fraction. Three and three quarters is three times four plus three, over four, which is fifteen quarters.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Nine and three fifths is nine times five plus three, over five, which is forty eight fifths.

marks.area: the area is written as the product of the two fractions
marks.pairs: the tops fifteen and forty eight and the bottoms four and five are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='area'/>Step two, the area is length times breadth, fifteen quarters times forty eight fifths.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>That is fifteen times forty eight over four times five.

beats.on_screen: 15 and 5 share the factor 5: 15 becomes 3, 5 becomes 1; 48 and 4 share the factor 4: 48 becomes 12, 4 becomes 1; the working shows (3 × 12)/(1 × 1)

marks.first: the fifteen and the five are linked by a line
marks.res1: the three and the one replace them
marks.second: the forty eight and the four are linked by a second line
marks.res2: the twelve and the one replace them

beats.colours: the first pair in the accent colour and the second pair in a second colour
beats.moves_through: the numbers change in both pairs
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, fifteen and five share the factor five, so divide both by five.
<bookmark mark='res1'/>The fifteen becomes three, and the five becomes one.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Forty eight and four share the factor four, so divide both by four.
<bookmark mark='res2'/>The forty eight becomes twelve, and the four becomes one.

marks.mult: the tops and the bottoms are multiplied
marks.unit: the unit square feet is written beside the working

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step four, multiply what is left, three times twelve over one times one.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>The sides are in feet, so the area is in square feet.

beats.on_screen: check: 3 3/4 is a little less than 4 and 9 3/5 is a little less than 10, so the area is a little less than 40

marks.near: each side is rounded up to the next whole number
marks.less: the product of the two whole numbers is shown beside the area

narration: <bookmark mark='near'/>Step five, check the size. Three and three quarters is a little less than four.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Nine and three fifths is a little less than ten. The area is a little less than forty.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed with its unit

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The area of the rectangle is thirty six square feet.
